Combined Energy Category Share (post Alani Nu)
Accretive to revenue and EPS year one
UBS fireside chat; management addressed head-on the energy-category slowdown and Celsius's own market-share erosion.

Category went negative for the first time in Q3 2024 amid macro pressure, slowing convenience traffic and shifting consumer habits; competitors 'woke up' with their largest-ever sugar-free innovation push.
CEO Fieldly candidly admitted 'we're not happy where we ended 2024 out and share' and that Celsius 'could have timed our innovation better.'
Deliberate slower Q1 2025 start: a 'step change' shifting innovation timing from mid-January to mid-April; explicit lever for the back-half recovery.
Structural shift to sugar-free (now the majority of the category) aligns with Celsius's all-sugar-free portfolio.
Expected 15%-20% spring-reset shelf-space gains (sold in last year); targeting 15,000+ incremental coolers within six feet of every checkout.
Pepsi partnership strengthening - hired 27-year PepsiCo veteran Eric Hanson (starting March 24); sales force now fully app-integrated; 2024 inventory optimization now behind the company.
Convenience-channel share lags total-company share (c-store was last channel entered, Circle K only mid-2022); 7-Eleven share already exceeds the ~11 company share.
CFO framed 2025 as a building year - softer first half, accelerating second half; gross margin 'circled' at ~50%; S&M between historical 22-23% and elevated 26% of 2024.
Tariffs: newly imposed 25% tariff flagged as a swing factor management declined to model given volatility; center of excellence provides ingredient-route mitigation.
Alani Nu positioned as incremental (only ~15% Celsius/Alani consumer overlap, lower than Red Bull/Monster overlap); deal makes Celsius a 'mega number three player' at ~16.5 combined share.
Asked, with hindsight, why the energy category slowed so unexpectedly in 2024.

2024 began strongly with record distribution gains, but category went negative for the first time in Q3 amid macro pressure, slowing convenience traffic and shifting consumer habits. Celsius peaked near a 12 share (now ~11 ex coffees/teas). Competitors 'woke up' with their largest-ever sugar-free innovation push. Bright spot: structural shift to majority sugar-free. Light back-half 2024 innovation and timing drove soft trailing scans.
Market-Share Evolution & What Could Be Done Differently
Asked what did not play out as planned with the expected convenience reset share lift and what Celsius could have done differently.

Candidly said 'we're not happy where we ended 2024 out and share'; competition leaned in and Celsius 'could have timed our innovation better.' 2025 fix: a step change in innovation timing (causing the slower Q1 start), an internal growth department synergizing marketing and sales, better retail execution, and converting strong household awareness into higher purchase consideration and frequency.
Drivers of Category Improvement & 2025 Run Rate
Asked what is driving recent category improvement and whether mid-to-high single-digit growth is a fair 2025 run rate given tougher summer comps.

Anticipates mid-to-high single-digit category growth through the year (consistent with Mintel and internal numbers), cautiously optimistic. Improvement driven by consumers returning after a tough Q3; energy shifting from impulse purchase to pantry/multi-pack staple; usage occasions expanding (energy replacing coffee; Subway up to 18,000 locations; Jersey Mike's; Pepsi foodservice).
Asked to elaborate on the expected 15%-20% spring-reset space gain and whether soft core-brand velocities are causing any retailer to pull back shelf space.

Reiterated Celsius is 'here to win' with ~1,000 dedicated team members; 10-share crossed, 15 the next hurdle (citing South Florida 20%+, NYC near 20, Baltimore 18, Buffalo/LA/Chicago north of 15). Conceded that failure to grow share/revenue would bring 'hard decisions' at year-end buyer meetings, but said soft 4-/12-week reads reflect the innovation-timing step change and does not anticipate those conversations.
Asked how Celsius plans to close the gap between total-company share and lower convenience-store share as it expands TDP.

Convenience was the last channel Celsius entered (built food, gyms, Amazon, large format, drug first), so long runway. Partnering with major/regional c-store chains on food-pairing collaborations (7-Eleven, AMPM). CFO Langhans noted 7-Eleven share already exceeds the ~11 company share - proof Celsius can win in national convenience over time.
Asked what is unique about the Celsius consumer versus legacy energy - usage occasions, frequency, loyalty, switching - and whether the consumer is more discretionary.

Celsius consumer is core to a daily routine, wanting 'more out of their energy drink' - no crash/jitters, great flavor, enhanced vitamins ('a multivitamin in a can,' 2.8g of vitamins). Large share are fitness advocates/athletes; high repurchase. Some consumers move between Red Bull and Monster on promotion/pricing/flavor, but Celsius has an extremely loyal following. Category could evolve toward CSD-like daily-staple status over 5-20 years.
Asked how Celsius is strengthening the Pepsi relationship after 2024's incentive-structure changes and inventory surprises, plus inventory-optimization color.

Described a strong, deepening Pepsi relationship - tied into priority periods/strategic planning, treated like Pepsi's own brands, leveraging 30,000+ reps, strengthened by Eric Hanson's hire. CFO Langhans said the 400-500-strong sales force is fully app-integrated; current depletions consistent with scanner data, no inventory issues to call out. 2024's significant Pepsi footprint optimization is now behind the company.
Asked to conceptually frame US core-Celsius top-line growth given lapping of 2024 inventory destocking and promotional impacts.

CFO Langhans said first half of 2025 is a tougher comp than the back half (2024 retail growth ~22% stronger in front half). Q3 2024 inventory movement means a 'big pick up' in Q3 2025. Innovation moving to mid-April and promotional calendar skewed late Q1/Q2 concentrate comp pressure in Q1; easier reported comps begin ~May. Cadence: first-half softness then second/third-quarter acceleration.
Asked about the 2025 innovation plan, the Hydration sticks opportunity, and room to expand into other adjacent categories.

2025 core/Vibe/Essentials innovation is flavor-led (mango lemonade for summer, Retro Vibe, Playa Vibe, Grape Slush on Essentials, plus a back-half LTO). First adjacency move is Hydration, launched on Amazon, rolling to Walmart.com and other retailers - 'too early to tell' on size. Powder/energy-stick business is 'almost $100M' and growing. Cautious on brand stretch - 'we got to win in energy' first.
Asked what Celsius has learned in new international markets and whether future growth comes more from new markets or deeper distribution within existing ones.

US health-and-wellness trends are global. Celsius has a 13-14 share in Sweden (first international market, 10+ years), high single digits in Finland. Recent launches (UK, Ireland, Australia, NZ, France) follow a methodical, profitability-conscious, English-speaking-market approach with partner Centauri. Australia (7-Eleven lead launch) 'one of the best launches they've seen in 5-7 years.' Further expansion likely in 2026-2027.
Asked for high-level thoughts on the Alani Nu brand and how it is positioned in the energy category.

Celsius has admired Alani Nu for years; resonates with a unique, loyal female/Gen Z new-to-category consumer. Combined entity is a 'mega number three player' at over a 16.5 energy share, unlocking multi-brand pricing/promotional flexibility, supplier and infrastructure synergies. Reiterated the deal is accretive to revenue and EPS in year one.
Asked whether there is brand overlap given both brands' health-and-wellness roots, and where the biggest integration synergies lie.

Rejected the cannibalization thesis: Celsius is ~50-50 male/female; only ~15% of Celsius consumers also buy Alani Nu - lower than overlap with Red Bull or Monster - so it is incremental. CFO Langhans said the biggest synergy is bringing Alani Nu into Celsius's built-up infrastructure (500-person sales force, key-accounts team, supply chain, center of excellence), with workforce, supply-chain, procurement and back-office savings largely 'known cost' that can be lined up in the second half.
Asked how gross margin and profitability evolve over the next 12 months given aluminum and tariff pressures.

CFO Langhans said price slots in place leave Celsius comfortable on 2024-set pricing. Big Beverages and scale create upside on the 50% margin; tariffs could drive downside, so management 'circled' 50% with both upside and downside. Declined to model the 25% tariff given volatility; center of excellence provides alternative ingredient channels. Big Beverages will continue to unlock raw-material/ingredient-route optimization.
Asked what a reasonable 2025 S&M spend target is, given 2024's 26% of revenue included both stepped-up investment and deleverage.

CFO Langhans said S&M historically closer to 22-23%, spiked to 26% in 2024. For 2025, will invest behind the brand where opportunity exists, with quarterly variation (Q1/Q4 higher as % of revenue given lower seasonal revenue). Fieldly added the new summer 'healthy Halo' program, broader distribution and strong innovation mean spend could land at the higher end - 2025 is the time to invest given peak ACV and retailer lean-in.
